First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by $3{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}4y-1 & >\frac{5y-2}{3} \\ 3\cdot (4y-1) & >3\cdot (\frac{5y-2}{3}) \\ 3\cdot (4y-1) & >\cancel{3}\cdot (\frac{5y-2}{\cancel{3}}) \\ 3\cdot (4y-1) & >5y-2 \\ 12y-3 & >5y-2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\eqalign{
		12y-3	&> 5y-2 \[5pt]
		12y-3-5y	&> 5y-2-5y \[5pt]
		7y-3	&> {-2} \[5pt]
		7y-3 +3	&> {-2} +3 \[5pt]
		7y		&> {1} \[5pt]
		\dfrac{7y}{7}	&> \dfrac{1}7 \[5pt]
		y		&> \dfrac{1}{7}
	}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y > \dfrac17.$
